--- title: "[BetaLS]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Beta family for GAMLSS with mean-precision parameterisation. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta_ls.py#L12-L300){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python BetaLS() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `BetaLS` extends the plain `Beta` family by letting both the mean `mu` and the precision `phi` vary smoothly with covariates, rather than treating precision as a single estimated constant. Use it for responses strictly between 0 and 1 (rates, proportions, fractions) where not only the typical level but also how tightly the response clusters around that level changes across the range of the predictors — for example, a proportion that becomes more variable in some regions of the covariate space and more tightly concentrated in others. The mean uses the logit link (as in `Beta`) and the precision uses the log link, keeping `mu` in `(0, 1)` and `phi > 0`. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The two parameters use distinct link functions: $$ g_{\mu}(\mu) = \log\!\left(\frac{\mu}{1-\mu}\right), \qquad g_{\phi}(\phi) = \log(\phi). $$ If `a = mu * phi` and `b = (1 - mu) * phi`, the response follows `y ~ Beta(a, b)` with density $$ f(y \mid \mu, \phi) = \frac{y^{a-1}(1-y)^{b-1}}{B(a, b)}, \qquad a = \mu\phi,\ \ b = (1-\mu)\phi. $$ As in `Beta`, larger `phi` concentrates the distribution more tightly around `mu` (`Var(Y) = mu(1-mu) / (1+phi)`), but here `phi` is itself modeled as a smooth function of covariates rather than a single scalar. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAMLSS where both the mean and precision of a proportion response vary smoothly: ::: {#124c8b40 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk from scipy.special import expit rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = expit(np.sin(x)) phi = 10.0 + 15.0 * np.abs(np.cos(x)) y = rng.beta(mu * phi, (1 - mu) * phi) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAMLSS( formulas={"mu": "y ~ s(x)", "phi": "y ~ s(x)"}, family=wk.BetaLS(), ) model.fit(data) print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAMLSS fit summary ======================================== Family: BetaLS(mu=logit, phi=log) N obs: 300 Global deviance: -548.1336 AIC: -521.9058 BIC: -473.3348 Log-likelihood: 274.0668 Converged: True (6 iterations) --- mu --- EDF total: 6.37 Smooth 1: edf = 5.37 --- phi --- EDF total: 6.74 Smooth 1: edf = 5.74 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
parameter_names Names of the distributional parameters modeled by `BetaLS`.
### [parameter_names]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Names of the distributional parameters modeled by `BetaLS`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [parameter_names]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[str, ...]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
d2l_dtheta2() Expected Fisher information for `mu` or `phi`.
dl_dtheta() First derivative of the Beta log-likelihood with respect to `mu` or `phi`.
initialize() Starting values for `mu` and `phi` from the raw response.
link() Apply the link function for `mu` or `phi`.
link_derivative() Derivative of the link function for `mu` or `phi`.
link_inverse() Apply the inverse link for `mu` or `phi`.

### [d2l_dtheta2()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Expected Fisher information for `mu` or `phi`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta_ls.py#L189-L223){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python d2l_dtheta2(param, y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} With `a = mu * phi`, `b = (1 - mu) * phi`, and trigamma function $\psi_1$: $$ -E\!\left[\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = \phi^2\big(\psi_1(a) + \psi_1(b)\big), \qquad -E\!\left[\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \phi^2}\right] = \mu^2 \psi_1(a) + (1-\mu)^2 \psi_1(b) - \psi_1(\phi). $$ ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"phi"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)` (unused, kept for interface consistency). [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"phi"`, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise working weights, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [dl_dtheta()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} First derivative of the Beta log-likelihood with respect to `mu` or `phi`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta_ls.py#L152-L187){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python dl_dtheta(param, y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} With `a = mu * phi`, `b = (1 - mu) * phi`, `y* = logit(y)`, and `mu* = psi(a) - psi(b)` (where $\psi$ is the digamma function), the score functions are $$ \frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \phi\,(y^{*} - \mu^{*}), \qquad \frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \phi} = \mu\,(y^{*} - \mu^{*}) + \psi(\phi) - \psi(b) + \log(1 - y). $$ ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"phi"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values in `(0, 1)`, shape `(n,)`. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"phi"`, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise first derivatives, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Starting values for `mu` and `phi` from the raw response. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta_ls.py#L249-L273){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `mu` is initialized at the observed values themselves (clipped to `[0.01, 0.99]` to stay strictly inside the unit interval), and `phi` at a method-of-moments estimate of the precision derived from the sample mean and variance of `y` (clamped to at least `1.0`), constant across observations. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values in `(0, 1)`, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `{"mu": y_safe.copy(), "phi": }`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the link function for `mu` or `phi`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta_ls.py#L83-L104){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link(param, values) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `mu` uses the logit link, keeping its additive predictor unconstrained while `link_inverse` maps it back into `(0, 1)`; `phi` uses the log link, keeping it positive. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"phi"`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Parameter values on the natural scale, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `logit(values)` for `"mu"`, `log(values)` for `"phi"`. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the link function for `mu` or `phi`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta_ls.py#L129-L150){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_derivative(param, values) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For the logit link, $d\eta/d\mu = 1/(\mu(1-\mu))$; for the log link, $d\eta/d\phi = 1/\phi$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"phi"`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Parameter values on the natural scale at which to evaluate the derivative, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `1 / (values * (1 - values))` for `"mu"`, `1 / values` for `"phi"`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the inverse link for `mu` or `phi`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta_ls.py#L106-L127){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_inverse(param, eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Maps the additive predictor back to the natural scale: the logistic (`expit`) function for `mu`, restoring `(0, 1)`, and the exponential for `phi`, restoring positivity. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"phi"`. [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Additive predictor values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `expit(eta)` for `"mu"`, `exp(eta)` for `"phi"`. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Total Beta log-likelihood at the current `mu` and `phi`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta_ls.py#L225-L247){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python log_likelihood(y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Evaluated using the shape parameterization `a = mu * phi`, `b = (1 - mu) * phi`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values in `(0, 1)`, shape `(n,)`. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"phi"`, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The log-likelihood summed over all observations. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate response values from a Beta distribution with the given `mu`, `phi`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta_ls.py#L275-L297){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate(params, rng) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Converts to the shape parameterization (`a = mu * phi`, `b = (1 - mu) * phi`) expected by `rng.beta`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"phi"`, each of shape `(n,)`. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [np.random.Generator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A NumPy random generator used to draw the simulated values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated response values in `(0, 1)`, shape `(n,)`. :::
